cor-rv-quadform-special.html:
Under the conditions of @thm-rv-quadform-mean:

  1. E[(Y−b)⊤A(Y−b)]=tr(AΣ)+(μ−b)⊤A(μ−b) for any constant b;

  2. if Σ=σ2I, then E(Y⊤AY)=σ2tr(A)+μ⊤Aμ;

  3. if Σ is positive definite, the squared Mahalanobis distance @eq-rv-mahalanobis has EΔ2(Y)=p;

  4. for random vectors U (p×1) and V (q×1) with finite second moments and a constant p×q matrix A, E(U⊤AV)=tr(ACov(V,U))+E(U)⊤AE(V).

def-rv-correlation.title: Correlation matrix
def-rv-correlation.html: Let Y have covariance matrix Σ=(σij) with every σii>0, and let Dσ=diag(σ111/2,…,σpp1/2) be the diagonal matrix of standard deviations. The correlation matrix of Y is R=Dσ−1ΣDσ−1,with entriesρij=σijσiiσjj=corr(Yi,Yj). Equivalently Σ=DσRDσ. For random vectors U and V with standard-deviation matrices DU and DV, the cross-correlation matrix is DU−1Cov(U,V)DV−1.

def-rv-expectation.title: Expectation of a random matrix
def-rv-expectation.html: A random matrix Z=(Zij) is an m×k array of random variables. If every Zij has a finite expectation, the expectation of Z is the m×k matrix of expectations, E(Z)=(E(Zij)). A random vector is the case k=1.

def-rv-mean-cov.title: Mean vector and covariance matrices
def-rv-mean-cov.html: Let Y be a p×1 random vector with finite second moments. Its mean vector is μ=E(Y), and its covariance matrix is the p×p matrix Cov(Y)=E[(Y−μ)(Y−μ)⊤], whose (i,j) entry is σij=Cov(Yi,Yj) and whose diagonal holds the variances σii=Var(Yi). If U (p×1) and V (q×1) both have finite second moments, their cross-covariance matrix is the p×q matrix Cov(U,V)=E[(U−EU)(V−EV)⊤], with (i,j) entry Cov(Ui,Vj).

def-rv-mgf.title: Moment generating function
def-rv-mgf.html: The moment generating function of a p×1 random vector Y is MY(t)=Eexp⁡(t⊤Y),t∈Rp, where the expectation may be +∞. We say that MY exists if it is finite for all t in some neighbourhood {‖t‖<h} of the origin, h>0.

eq-rv-linear-combination.html: Var(a⊤Y)=a⊤Σa=∑i=1p∑j=1paiajσij,Cov(a⊤Y,b⊤Y)=a⊤Σb.

eq-rv-mahalanobis.html: Δ2(Y)=(Y−μ)⊤Σ−1(Y−μ),

eq-rv-rss-mean.html: E(RSS)=σ2(n−r)+‖(I−M)θ‖2.

exm-rv-centering.title: Centring a sample
exm-rv-centering.html: Let Y be n×1 with Cov(Y)=σ2In, and write J=11⊤. The mean is Y¯=n−11⊤Y, and the vector of deviations is d=(I−n−1J)Y. The matrix I−n−1J is symmetric and idempotent, so @thm-rv-linear gives Cov(d)=σ2(I−n−1J),Cov(Y¯,d)=σ2n−11⊤(I−n−1J)=0⊤. The deviations have variances σ2(1−1/n) and are negatively correlated, with correlation −1/(n−1) between each pair, because they are forced to sum to zero. And each deviation is uncorrelated with the mean. Under normality, uncorrelated becomes independent (@exm-mvn-mean-deviations), which is the first half of @cor-qf-sample-variance.

exm-rv-circle.title: A point on a circle
exm-rv-circle.html: Let Θ be uniform on [0,2π) and Y=(cos⁡Θ,sin⁡Θ)⊤. Then E(cos⁡Θ)=E(sin⁡Θ)=0, E(cos2⁡Θ)=E(sin2⁡Θ)=12, and E(cos⁡Θsin⁡Θ)=12E(sin⁡2Θ)=0. So μ=0 and Cov(Y)=12I2, exactly the moments of two independent coordinates. Yet Y12+Y22=1: once Y1 is known, Y2 is known up to sign. Covariance measures linear association only, and the dependence here is entirely nonlinear.

exm-rv-longley.title: Macroeconomic series
exm-rv-longley.html:
Longley’s data give n=16 annual observations (1947–1962) on p=7 US series: total employment, the GNP deflator, GNP, unemployment, armed forces, population and the year. The eigenvalues of S run from 9.94×109 down to 1.07×10−2, a ratio of 9.3×1011. That spread says little about the structure of the data. It mostly reflects units: the standard deviation of GNP is 99395, that of the deflator 10.79.

The correlation matrix removes the units (@prp-rv-correlation(d)). Its eigenvalues sum to p=7. The largest is 5.533, so one direction carries about 79% of the standardized variation, and the smallest is 2.59×10−4. By @thm-mat-extremal-rayleigh, the unit vector v belonging to the smallest eigenvalue minimizes the sample variance of v⊤z over standardized combinations. Its two largest weights are 0.681 on year and −0.674 on GNP, and the combination has standard deviation 0.016, against 1 for each standardized variable. In these sixteen years GNP is almost an exact linear function of time (their correlation is 0.995). This is the sample version of @thm-rv-cov-nnd(c): a nearly zero eigenvalue marks a nearly constant linear combination. For regression it signals collinearity, which Chapter 26 studies. Finally, the first 5 rows alone give a sample covariance matrix of rank 4, as @prp-rv-sample-moments(c) requires.

exm-rv-multinomial.title: Multinomial counts
exm-rv-multinomial.html: In m independent trials, each outcome falls into one of k categories with probabilities π=(π1,…,πk)⊤, where ∑jπj=1. Let Zt be the indicator vector of trial t, with a single 1 in the position of its category. Then E(Zt)=π, and ZtZt⊤=diag(Zt) because the indicator has only one nonzero entry. So Cov(Zt)=diag(π)−ππ⊤. The count vector Y=∑tZt is a sum of independent vectors, and @prp-rv-sums(c) gives Σ=Cov(Y)=m(diag(π)−ππ⊤). Because Σ1=m(π−ππ⊤1)=0, the matrix is singular, and @thm-rv-cov-nnd(c) recovers the constraint 1⊤Y=m. For m=20 and π=(0.5,0.3,0.2)⊤ the eigenvalues are 7.762, 4.638 and 0. All 5000 simulated count vectors lie in the plane μ+C(Σ)={y:1⊤y=m}.

exm-rv-pairwise.title: Pairwise but not mutually independent
exm-rv-pairwise.html: Let S1 and S2 be independent, each equal to ±1 with probability 12, and put S3=S1S2. Each Sj is ±1 with probability 12. Each pair is independent: for instance, Pr(S1=s,S3=u)=Pr(S1=s,S2=su)=14 for all signs s,u. So Cov(S)=I3. But the three are not mutually independent, since S3 is a function of the other two. A third-order moment shows the failure directly: E(S1S2S3)=1, whereas mutual independence would force it to be 0. No condition on the covariance matrix can detect this, because covariances involve only pairs.

exm-rv-random-intercept.title: A shared random effect
exm-rv-random-intercept.html: Measurements Y1,…,Yk on the same subject share a subject effect: Y=α1+ε, where α has variance τ2, Cov(ε)=σ2Ik, and ε is independent of α with mean zero. Given α, the mean is α1 and the covariance is σ2I. By @prp-rv-total-covariance, Cov(Y)=σ2Ik+τ211⊤, so every pair of measurements has correlation τ2/(τ2+σ2). Independent errors combined with a shared random component produce exactly this equicorrelation structure. It is the starting point of Chapter 32. Ordinary least squares ignores it, with consequences that Chapter 33 examines.

exm-rv-rss-bias.title: Residual sum of squares under a wrong mean
exm-rv-rss-bias.title_html: Residual sum of squares under a wrong mean
exm-rv-rss-bias.html:
Let Cov(Y)=σ2In and E(Y)=θ, where θ need not lie in C(X). The residual sum of squares is Y⊤(I−M)Y, where M is symmetric and idempotent of rank r=rank(X), so tr(I−M)=n−r (@thm-mat-idempotent). By @cor-rv-quadform-special(b), E(RSS)=σ2(n−r)+‖(I−M)θ‖2.{#eq-rv-rss-mean}

If the model is right, θ∈C(X), the second term vanishes and RSS/(n−r) is unbiased for σ2. If the model is wrong, the estimate is biased upwards by the squared distance from the true mean to the model space, divided by n−r. For instance, fit a straight line at x=1,…,6 when the true mean is the parabola θi=14(xi−3.5)2 and σ2=1. Then σ2(n−r)=4, ‖(I−M)θ‖2=2.333, and E(RSS)=6.333. Chapter 19 studies such departures systematically.

exm-rv-rss-variance.title: Skewed errors and a misspecified line
exm-rv-rss-variance.title_html: Skewed errors and a misspecified line
exm-rv-rss-variance.html: Continue @exm-rv-rss-bias, now with independent centred exponential errors, for which σ2=1, μ3=2 and μ4=9. @thm-rv-quadform-variance gives Var(RSS)=29.80. Of this, the kurtosis term contributes 16.73 and the skewness term −4.27. Normal errors with the same mean and variance would give 17.33, so the exponential errors multiply the variance by 1.72 even though the mean of RSS is unchanged. Over 106 simulated data sets, the variance of RSS is 30.04. The script also confirms the formula exactly for a two-point error distribution.

exm-rv-sample-variance.title: Sample variance with unequal means and variances
exm-rv-sample-variance.title_html: Sample variance with unequal means and variances
exm-rv-sample-variance.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be uncorrelated with means μi and variances σi2, and let S2=(n−1)−1Y⊤CY with C=I−n−1J. Here Σ=diag(σ12,…,σn2), so tr(CΣ)=(1−1/n)∑iσi2, and μ⊤Cμ=∑i(μi−μ¯)2. Therefore E(S2)=σ2―+1n−1∑i=1n(μi−μ¯)2,σ2―=1n∑i=1nσi2. With a common mean, S2 is unbiased for the average variance, even when the variances differ. Differences in the means inflate it. That is exactly why a residual mean square estimates σ2 only when the mean structure is right.

exm-rv-whitening.title: Two whitenings
exm-rv-whitening.html: Take μ=(3,1)⊤ and Σ=(42.42.42.25), so the standard deviations are 2 and 1.5 and the correlation is 0.8. The eigenvalues are 5.680 and 0.570. The symmetric and Cholesky whitening matrices are Σ−1/2=(0.717−0.425−0.4251.027),L−1=(0.5000−0.6671.111). The Cholesky version standardizes Y1 alone and then removes from Y2 its linear dependence on Y1, in the spirit of Gram–Schmidt. The symmetric version treats both coordinates alike and moves points as little as possible (@exr-rv-whitening-closest). Figure 2.2.1 applies both to 400 simulated points. The two whitened clouds differ by a rotation through 22.5∘, and every point keeps its Mahalanobis distance.

exr-rv-best-constant-matrix.title: B2
exr-rv-best-constant-matrix.html: Show that E[(Y−a)(Y−a)⊤]−Cov(Y) is nonnegative definite for every constant a, with equality iff a=μ. Deduce that a=μ minimizes E[(Y−a)⊤N(Y−a)] for every positive definite N.

exr-rv-best-quadratic.title: B5
exr-rv-best-quadratic.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be independent N(0,σ2). Among symmetric A with E(Y⊤AY)=σ2, show that Var(Y⊤AY) is minimized by A=n−1I. Hint: tr(A2)≥(trA)2/n.

exr-rv-blp-scalar.title: A1
exr-rv-blp-scalar.html: For scalar Y and X with Var(X)>0, show that the best linear predictor has slope σYX/σXX, and that its mean squared error is σYY(1−ρ2).

exr-rv-blp-singular.title: B2
exr-rv-blp-singular.html: Let X=(X1,X1)⊤ with Var(X1)=1, and let Cov(Y,X1)=c. Find two different generalized inverses of ΣXX that give different B∗, and show that both give the same predictor B∗(X−μX).

exr-rv-cholesky-residual.title: A2
exr-rv-cholesky-residual.html: For p=2 and Σ=LL⊤, show that the second component of L−1(Y−μ) is a multiple of Y2−μ2−(σ12/σ11)(Y1−μ1). Explain the connection with @thm-rv-blp.

exr-rv-correlation-angles.title: C1
exr-rv-correlation-angles.html: 1. Show that a p×p matrix is a correlation matrix iff it is the Gram matrix (ui⊤uj) of p unit vectors in Rp. (b) For p=3, write ρij=cos⁡ϑij with ϑij∈[0,π]. Show that @prp-rv-three-correlations is equivalent to the spherical triangle inequalities |ϑ12−ϑ13|≤ϑ23≤min(ϑ12+ϑ13,2π−ϑ12−ϑ13).

exr-rv-cov-quadforms.title: B4
exr-rv-cov-quadforms.html: Under the conditions of @thm-rv-quadform-variance with θ=0, show that Cov(Y⊤AY,Y⊤BY)=(μ4−3σ4)a⊤b+2σ4tr(AB), where a and b are the diagonals of the symmetric matrices A and B. Hint: apply the theorem to A+B.

exr-rv-cov-rank.title: B2
exr-rv-cov-rank.html: Show that C(AΣA⊤)=C(AΣ) for every nonnegative definite Σ and conformable A. Deduce that rankCov(AY)≤rankCov(Y).

exr-rv-differences.title: A1
exr-rv-differences.html: Let Cov(Y)=σ2I3. Find the covariance and correlation matrices of the successive differences (Y2−Y1,Y3−Y2)⊤, and of (Y2−Y1,Y3−Y2,Y3−Y1)⊤. Which is singular, and which linear combination is degenerate?

exr-rv-distance-two-vectors.title: A1
exr-rv-distance-two-vectors.html: For random vectors U and V of the same size, show that E‖U−V‖2=trCov(U)+trCov(V)−2trCov(U,V)+‖EU−EV‖2.

exr-rv-equicorrelation.title: A1
exr-rv-equicorrelation.html: Show that (1−ρ)Ip+ρ11⊤ is a correlation matrix iff −1/(p−1)≤ρ≤1. Explain the lower bound through the variance of ∑iZi.

exr-rv-expected-gram.title: A1
exr-rv-expected-gram.html: Let Z be an n×p random matrix whose entries are independent, with mean 0 and variance σ2. Show that E(Z⊤Z)=nσ2Ip and E(ZZ⊤)=pσ2In. For a constant p×p matrix B, find E(ZBZ⊤).

exr-rv-gls-cov.title: C1
exr-rv-gls-cov.html: In Y=Xβ+ε with X of full column rank, let Cov(ε)=σ2V with V positive definite. Find Cov(β^) for β^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤Y and Cov(β~) for β~=(X⊤V−1X)−1X⊤V−1Y. Show that Cov(β^)−Cov(β~) is nonnegative definite. Hint: show that β^−β~ and β~ are uncorrelated.

exr-rv-hadamard.title: B1
exr-rv-hadamard.html: Show that det(Σ)≤∏iσii for every covariance matrix, with equality for positive definite Σ iff Σ is diagonal. Hint: factor out Dσ and use the eigenvalues of R.

exr-rv-lag-quadform.title: B1
exr-rv-lag-quadform.html: Let E(Yt)=μ and Cov(Yt,Ys)=σ2ϕ|t−s| for t,s=1,…,n, with |ϕ|<1. Show that the sample variance satisfies E(S2)=σ2[1−2n(n−1)∑k=1n−1(n−k)ϕk]. Is S2 biased up or down when ϕ>0? What happens as n→∞ with ϕ fixed?

exr-rv-mgf-multinomial.title: A1
exr-rv-mgf-multinomial.html: Find the moment generating function of the multinomial count vector of @exm-rv-multinomial, and recover its mean and covariance matrix from @thm-rv-mgf(b).

exr-rv-mixture.title: B3
exr-rv-mixture.html: A random label K takes values 1,…,g with probabilities πk. Given K=k, Y has mean mk and covariance Σk. Show that Cov(Y)=∑kπkΣk+∑kπk(mk−m¯)(mk−m¯)⊤, where m¯=∑kπkmk. Interpret the two terms as within-group and between-group covariance.

exr-rv-moving-average.title: B1
exr-rv-moving-average.html: Let ε0,…,εn be uncorrelated with variance σ2, and let Yt=εt+θεt−1 for t=1,…,n. Find Cov(Y), and show that it is positive definite for every real θ, including θ=±1.

exr-rv-nonlinear.title: A2
exr-rv-nonlinear.html: Let X be uniform on (−1,1) and Y=X2+ε, with ε independent of X, mean 0 and variance σ2. Find the best linear predictor of Y from X and its mean squared error, and compare with the mean squared error of E(Y∣X).

exr-rv-pairwise-many.title: B1
exr-rv-pairwise-many.html: Let S1,…,Sk be independent random signs. For each nonempty A⊆{1,…,k} put TA=∏i∈ASi. Show that the 2k−1 variables TA are pairwise independent with covariance matrix I, and find a triple of them that is not mutually independent.

exr-rv-partial-three.title: B1
exr-rv-partial-three.html: Let (Y1,Y2,Y3) have correlation matrix R. Compute the partial covariance matrix of (Y2,Y3) given Y1 from @thm-rv-blp, and show that the corresponding correlation is ρ23−ρ12ρ13(1−ρ122)(1−ρ132).

exr-rv-rss-correlated.title: B2
exr-rv-rss-correlated.html: Suppose E(Y)=Xβ and Cov(Y)=σ2V. Show that E(RSS)=σ2tr((I−M)V). For the equicorrelated V=(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤ and a model with 1∈C(X), show that E(RSS)/(n−r)=σ2(1−ρ).

exr-rv-sample-serial.title: B1
exr-rv-sample-serial.html: Suppose the rows of Y are observed in time order, with common mean μ and covariance Σ, and that neighbouring rows are correlated: Cov(yi,yi+1)=ρΣ, while Cov(yi,yj)=0 for |i−j|≥2. Show that E(S)=(1−2ρ/n)Σ and Cov(y¯)=n−2[n+2(n−1)ρ]Σ. Which of the two effects disappears as n→∞?

exr-rv-schur-nnd.title: C1
exr-rv-schur-nnd.html: Let N be the symmetric partitioned matrix N=(ΣYYΣYXΣXYΣXX). Show that N is nonnegative definite iff ΣXX is nonnegative definite, C(ΣXY)⊆C(ΣXX), and ΣYY−ΣYXΣXX−ΣXY is nonnegative definite for some generalized inverse ΣXX− (equivalently, given the column-space condition, for every one). Show by a 2×2 example that the column-space condition cannot be dropped.

exr-rv-sign-product.title: B1
exr-rv-sign-product.html: Let X have a distribution symmetric about 0 with Var(X)=1 and EX4<∞, let S be independent of X with Pr(S=1)=Pr(S=−1)=12, and put Y=(X,SX)⊤. Show that the two components have the same distribution and are uncorrelated, and that Cov(Y12,Y22)=Var(X2). Deduce that Y1 and Y2 are independent iff X is itself a random sign. (Chapter 3 takes X standard normal.)

exr-rv-singular-whitening.title: B4
exr-rv-singular-whitening.html: Let Σ=Cov(Y) have rank r, with spectral decomposition Σ=ΓrΛrΓr⊤, where Γr⊤Γr=Ir and Λr holds the positive eigenvalues. Show that Z=Λr−1/2Γr⊤(Y−μ) has Cov(Z)=Ir and that Y=μ+ΓrΛr1/2Z with probability one. Show that (Y−μ)⊤Σ+(Y−μ)=‖Z‖2, where Σ+ is the Moore–Penrose inverse, and that its expectation is r.

exr-rv-var-sample-variance.title: B3
exr-rv-var-sample-variance.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be independent and identically distributed with variance σ2 and finite fourth central moment μ4. Use @thm-rv-quadform-variance to show that Var(S2)=(μ4−3σ4)/n+2σ4/(n−1). Compare with the normal case.

exr-rv-whitening-closest.title: B3
exr-rv-whitening-closest.html: Let Σ be positive definite. Among all W with WΣW⊤=I, show that E‖W(Y−μ)−(Y−μ)‖2 is minimized uniquely by W=Σ−1/2. Hint: use @prp-rv-whitening(b) and show that tr(QΣ1/2)≤tr(Σ1/2) for orthogonal Q.

prp-rv-correlation.title: Properties of correlation matrices
prp-rv-correlation.html:
Let R be the correlation matrix of Y.

  1. R is the covariance matrix of the standardized vector Z=Dσ−1(Y−μ). Hence R is nonnegative definite with unit diagonal, and tr(R)=p.

  2. |ρij|≤1, with |ρij|=1 iff Zj=ρijZi with probability one.

  3. rank(R)=rank(Σ). In particular, R is positive definite iff Σ is.

  4. If Y∗=DY+c with D=diag(d1,…,dp) and every di≠0, then ρij∗=sign(didj)ρij. Positive rescaling and shifting leave R unchanged.

  5. Conversely, every nonnegative definite matrix with unit diagonal is the correlation matrix of some random vector.

prp-rv-cov-basic.title: Elementary properties
prp-rv-cov-basic.html:
Let Y, U, V have finite second moments, with μ=E(Y) and Σ=Cov(Y), and let a, b be constant vectors of matching sizes. Then:

  1. Σ is symmetric;

  2. Cov(U,V)=E(UV⊤)−E(U)E(V)⊤, and in particular Σ=E(YY⊤)−μμ⊤;

  3. Cov(V,U)=Cov(U,V)⊤;

  4. Cov(U+a,V+b)=Cov(U,V);

  5. E[(Y−a)(Y−a)⊤]=Σ+(μ−a)(μ−a)⊤, and hence E‖Y−a‖2=tr(Σ)+‖μ−a‖2.

prp-rv-cramer-wold.title: Distributions are determined by linear combinations
prp-rv-cramer-wold.title_html: Distributions are determined by linear combinations
prp-rv-cramer-wold.html: If a⊤Y and a⊤V have the same distribution for every a∈Rp, then Y and V have the same distribution.

prp-rv-expectation-linear.title: Linearity of expectation
prp-rv-expectation-linear.html:
Let Z and Z2 be m×k random matrices with integrable entries, and let A (l×m), B (k×s) and C (l×s) be constant matrices. Then

  1. E(AZB+C)=AE(Z)B+C;

  2. E(Z+Z2)=E(Z)+E(Z2) and E(Z⊤)=E(Z)⊤;

  3. if m=k, then Etr(Z)=trE(Z).

prp-rv-multiple-correlation.title: Multiple correlation
prp-rv-multiple-correlation.html: Let Y be scalar with σYY=Var(Y)>0, let ΣXX be positive definite, and write σXY=Cov(X,Y). Over all a≠0, maxacorr(Y,a⊤X)2=ρY⋅X2=σXY⊤ΣXX−1σXYσYY, attained at a=ΣXX−1σXY, the coefficients of the best linear predictor (if σXY=0, every a attains the maximum 0). Moreover 1−ρY⋅X2=σYY⋅X/σYY.

prp-rv-sample-moments.title: Moments of sample moments
prp-rv-sample-moments.html:
Suppose the rows yi are pairwise uncorrelated random vectors with common mean μ and common covariance matrix Σ. Then

  1. E(y¯)=μ and Cov(y¯)=Σ/n;

  2. E(S)=Σ;

  3. S is nonnegative definite, and rank(S)≤min(p,n−1) for every realization.

prp-rv-sums.title: Covariance of sums
prp-rv-sums.html:
Let U,U2,V have finite second moments, with U and U2 of the same size in (a), and U and V of the same size in (b). Then

  1. Cov(U+U2,V)=Cov(U,V)+Cov(U2,V);

  2. Cov(U+V)=Cov(U)+Cov(U,V)+Cov(V,U)+Cov(V);

  3. if Y1,…,Yn are pairwise uncorrelated p×1 vectors and c1,…,cn are constants, then Cov(∑iciYi)=∑ici2Cov(Yi). In particular, if every Cov(Yi)=Σ, then Cov(Y¯)=Σ/n.

prp-rv-three-correlations.title: Three correlations
prp-rv-three-correlations.html: Let |ρ12|<1 and |ρ13|<1. The matrix R=(1ρ12ρ13ρ121ρ23ρ13ρ231) is a correlation matrix iff ρ12ρ13−(1−ρ122)(1−ρ132)≤ρ23≤ρ12ρ13+(1−ρ122)(1−ρ132).

prp-rv-total-covariance.title: Laws of total expectation and covariance
prp-rv-total-covariance.title_html: Laws of total expectation and covariance
prp-rv-total-covariance.html: If Y has finite second moments, then E(Y)=E[E(Y∣X)] and Cov(Y)=E[Cov(Y∣X)]+Cov(E(Y∣X)).

prp-rv-whitening.title: Whitening
prp-rv-whitening.html:
Let Σ=Cov(Y) be positive definite, with E(Y)=μ.

  1. Z=Σ−1/2(Y−μ) has E(Z)=0 and Cov(Z)=Ip.

  2. A p×p matrix W satisfies WΣW⊤=Ip iff W=QΣ−1/2 for some orthogonal Q. In particular, if Σ=LL⊤ is the Cholesky factorization, W=L−1 is such a matrix.

  3. For every W as in (b), ‖W(Y−μ)‖2=(Y−μ)⊤Σ−1(Y−μ).

thm-rv-blp.title: Best linear predictor
thm-rv-blp.html:
In the setting of @thm-rv-partitioned, fix a generalized inverse ΣXX− and put B∗=ΣYXΣXX−,E=Y−μY−B∗(X−μX),ΣYY⋅X=ΣYY−ΣYXΣXX−ΣXY.

  1. E(E)=0 and Cov(E,X)=0.

  2. Cov(E)=ΣYY⋅X. This matrix is nonnegative definite and does not depend on the choice of generalized inverse. Neither does B∗(X−μX), with probability one.

  3. For every constant p×q matrix B and p×1 vector c, E[(Y−c−BX)(Y−c−BX)⊤]=ΣYY⋅X+(B−B∗)ΣXX(B−B∗)⊤+dd⊤, where d=μY−c−BμX. So the mean squared error matrix is never smaller, in the nonnegative definite ordering, than ΣYY⋅X. Equality holds iff c=μY−BμX and BΣXX=ΣYX.

thm-rv-cov-nnd.title: Covariance matrices
thm-rv-cov-nnd.html:
Let Y have finite second moments, mean μ and covariance matrix Σ.

  1. Σ is nonnegative definite.

  2. Conversely, every p×p nonnegative definite matrix is the covariance matrix of some random vector.

  3. For a constant a, Σa=0 iff a⊤Y=a⊤μ with probability one.

  4. Pr(Y−μ∈C(Σ))=1. If S is any subspace with Pr(Y−μ∈S)=1, then C(Σ)⊆S.

In particular, Σ is singular iff some nontrivial linear combination of Y is constant with probability one. Then Y lies, with probability one, in the affine subspace μ+C(Σ) of dimension rank(Σ)<p, and this is the smallest such flat.

thm-rv-linear.title: Moments of affine transformations
thm-rv-linear.html:
Let Y be a p×1 random vector with finite second moments, E(Y)=μ and Cov(Y)=Σ. Let A be k×p, B be m×p, and b be k×1, all constant. Then

  1. E(AY+b)=Aμ+b;

  2. Cov(AY+b)=AΣA⊤;

  3. Cov(AY,BY)=AΣB⊤.

More generally, if U and V have finite second moments and A, B, b, c are constants of conformable sizes, then Cov(AU+b,BV+c)=ACov(U,V)B⊤.

thm-rv-mgf.title: Properties of moment generating functions
thm-rv-mgf.html:
Suppose MY exists.

  1. Uniqueness. If MV also exists and MY=MV on a neighbourhood of 0, then Y and V have the same distribution.

  2. Moments. All moments of Y are finite. The gradient of MY at 0 is E(Y), and its Hessian at 0 is E(YY⊤). The Hessian of log⁡MY at 0 is Cov(Y).

  3. Affine maps. For a constant k×p matrix A and k×1 vector b, MAY+b(s)=exp⁡(s⊤b)MY(A⊤s).

  4. Independence. Partition Y=(Y1⊤,Y2⊤)⊤ and t=(t1⊤,t2⊤)⊤ conformably. Then Y1 and Y2 are independent iff MY(t)=MY1(t1)MY2(t2) for all t in a neighbourhood of 0.

thm-rv-partitioned.title: Partitioned moments
thm-rv-partitioned.html:
Let W=(Y⊤,X⊤)⊤ have finite second moments, and write E(W)=(μYμX),Cov(W)=(ΣYYΣYXΣXYΣXX).

  1. μY=E(Y), μX=E(X), ΣYY=Cov(Y), ΣXX=Cov(X), ΣYX=Cov(Y,X) is p×q, and ΣXY=ΣYX⊤.

  2. For constants A, B, c of conformable sizes, Cov(AY,BX)=AΣYXB⊤, and Cov(AY+BX+c)=AΣYYA⊤+AΣYXB⊤+BΣXYA⊤+BΣXXB⊤.

  3. C(ΣXY)⊆C(ΣXX) and C(ΣYX)⊆C(ΣYY). Equivalently, for every generalized inverse ΣXX−, ΣXXΣXX−ΣXY=ΣXY,ΣYXΣXX−ΣXX=ΣYX, and similarly with the roles of Y and X exchanged.

thm-rv-quadform-mean.title: Mean of a quadratic form
thm-rv-quadform-mean.html: Let Y be a p×1 random vector with finite second moments, E(Y)=μ and Cov(Y)=Σ, and let A be a constant p×p matrix. Then E(Y⊤AY)=tr(AΣ)+μ⊤Aμ.

thm-rv-quadform-variance.title: Variance of a quadratic form
thm-rv-quadform-variance.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be independent with means θ1,…,θn and common central moments σ2=E(Yi−θi)2, μ3=E(Yi−θi)3 and μ4=E(Yi−θi)4<∞. Let A be a constant symmetric n×n matrix, and let a=(a11,…,ann)⊤ be its diagonal. Then Var(Y⊤AY)=(μ4−3σ4)a⊤a+2σ4tr(A2)+4σ2θ⊤A2θ+4μ3θ⊤Aa.
